context.text: When a `WebSocketEndpoint` uses `encoding = "json"`, `decode()` expects either a text frame containing JSON or a binary frame containing UTF-8 JSON bytes
Previously, the `else` branch assumed `message["bytes"]` was present and valid UTF-8 whenever `text` was absent or None
This led to two failure modes that crashed the endpoint handler instead of closing cleanly:
If a client sent an empty receive event (`text: None, bytes: None`), `message["bytes"].decode(...)` raised `AttributeError` (or `KeyError` if absent)
If a client sent non-UTF-8 binary data, `decode()` raised an unhandled `UnicodeDecodeError`

In both cases, the unhandled exceptions bypassed the `WS_1003_UNSUPPORTED_DATA` closure and caused `dispatch()` to catch a general exception, close with `WS_1011_INTERNAL_ERROR`, and raise a server traceback

This ensures `bytes` is checked before decoding and catches `UnicodeDecodeError` to close with `WS_1003_UNSUPPORTED_DATA` and raise `RuntimeError("Malformed JSON data received.")`, aligning binary JSON error handling with text JSON
